title: Rate Limiter
description: Build a configurable rate limiter supporting both sliding window log and token bucket algorithms.

steps.title: Implement fixed window counter
steps.description: Write a `FixedWindowCounter` class that tracks requests per fixed time window. Constructor takes `windowMs` (window duration in ms) and `maxRequests`. Implement a `allow()` method that increments a counter for the current window and returns true if under the limit. Print the count and whether each request is allowed.
hints: Use the current timestamp divided by windowMs to determine the current window key
Reset the counter when a new window starts (different key than stored)
Return count <= maxRequests from the allow() method

verification.successMessage: Fixed window counter tracks requests and enforces the limit correctly!
verification.failureMessage: Print the current count and whether each request is allowed (true/false) as you call allow().

steps.title: Build sliding window log
steps.description: Implement a `SlidingWindowLog` class that maintains a sorted list of timestamped requests. On each `allow()` call, remove timestamps older than `windowMs`, add the current timestamp, and check if the count is within `maxRequests`. Print the number of requests in the current window and the allow decision.
hints: Store timestamps in an array sorted chronologically
On each call, filter out timestamps where (now - timestamp) > windowMs
Push the current timestamp, then check if array length <= maxRequests

verification.successMessage: Sliding window log accurately tracks requests across a moving time window!
verification.failureMessage: Print the number of requests currently in the window and whether the request is allowed.

steps.title: Implement token bucket algorithm
steps.description: Create a `TokenBucket` class with configurable `capacity` and `refillRate` (tokens per second). Maintain a `tokens` count and a `lastRefill` timestamp. Implement `allow()` that refills tokens based on elapsed time, consumes one token if available, and returns true. Print token count and allow status.
hints: Calculate tokens to add: elapsed seconds * refillRate, capped at capacity
If tokens >= 1, decrement by 1 and return true; otherwise return false
Update lastRefill timestamp on each call

verification.successMessage: Token bucket properly refills tokens over time and enforces capacity!
verification.failureMessage: Print the current token count and the allow decision after each call.

steps.title: Add per-user rate limiting
steps.description: Wrap your sliding window log in a `PerUserRateLimiter` class that takes a `userId` parameter alongside each request. Maintain a separate window per user using a Map or dictionary. Implement `allow(userId)` that returns true if the user is under their limit. Print the remaining quota for each user after each request.
hints: Use a Map where keys are userId strings and values are SlidingWindowLog instances
Create the per-user limiter lazily when a new userId is first seen

verification.successMessage: Per-user rate limiting tracks separate quotas for each user!
verification.failureMessage: Print 'user: <id>, remaining: <quota>' after each allow() call for different users.

steps.title: Implement rate limit headers
steps.description: Extend the rate limiter to return response headers. Create a `getHeaders()` method that returns an object with `X-RateLimit-Limit` (max requests), `X-RateLimit-Remaining` (requests left in window), and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (epoch ms when the window resets). Print the headers after each request.
hints: X-RateLimit-Limit is the maxRequests from the window config
X-RateLimit-Remaining is maxRequests minus current window count
X-RateLimit-Reset is the end timestamp of the current window

verification.successMessage: Rate limit headers are correctly calculated with limit, remaining, and reset values!
verification.failureMessage: Print all three rate limit headers after each request.

steps.title: Build a middleware wrapper
steps.description: Combine everything into a `rateLimiterMiddleware` function that takes a config object, returns a middleware function `(handler)` => `(userId)` => result. The middleware checks the rate limit, adds headers to the result, and either calls the handler or returns a 429 Too Many Requests response. Print the full response object for allowed and blocked requests.
hints: The middleware should return an object: { allowed, headers, data, statusCode }
When rate limited, set statusCode to 429 and data to an error message
Merge the rate limit headers into every response object

verification.successMessage: Middleware wrapper correctly allows requests under the limit and blocks with 429 over the limit!
verification.failureMessage: Print the full response object showing a successful request and a blocked 429 request.
